eagle_wings.description: In a post-apocalyptic world, a virus wipes out humanity. Survivors face roaming scavengers called Reapers. Protagonist Hig, a pilot, survived the flu but lost his wife

To crack that vault, these two mortals will pull off the impossible: pose as Immortals themselves. They gather six more misfi...

eagle_wings.title: The End Of Oak Street
eagle_wings.description: After a mysterious cosmic event rips Oak Street from suburbia and transports their neighborhood to someplace unknown, the Platt family soon discovers that their very survival depends on them sticking together as they navigate their now unrecognizable surroundings

eagle_wings.title: PAW Patrol: The Dino Movie
eagle_wings.description: The Paw Patrol lands on a mysterious dinosaur island after a storm, where they meet Rex, a stranded pup. When Humdinger's reckless mining triggers a volcano, the team faces their biggest rescue mission yet to save the island

eagle_wings.title: Spider-Man: Brand New Day
eagle_wings.description: It's a BRAND NEW DAY for Peter Parker. Fighting crime full-time as Spider-Man in a world that doesn’t remember him -- and the pressure of seeing his old friends move on without him -- sparks a change in Peter he may not have the power to control. But that transformation might als...

eagle_wings.title: The Odyssey
eagle_wings.description: After the Trojan War, Odysseus faces a dangerous voyage back to Ithaca, meeting creatures like the Cyclops Polyphemus, Sirens, and Circe along the way

filmhouse.title: Singapore Minstrel (10th Anniversary)
filmhouse.description: A fantasy-documentary painting the magical universe of Singapore’s wildest busker Roy Payamal is the wildest busker of a country ranked the world’s most emotionless society. He takes his undermined line of work as a serious art- but is his faith impossible idealism or an admirable conviction? Singapore Minstrel is an invitation into his beautiful mind, a magical, trying universe where art and life dialogue in a tropical dream. In English with English subtitles. Rated PG. Join us for a live Q&A with director Salty Xi Jie Ng and artist Roy Payamal on Sat 5 September. Salty Xi Jie Ng is an artist, performer, educator, and mystic based between Singapore and Portland, Oregon. Her transdisciplinary practice is a collaborative, alchemical site intimately exploring the erotic, ancestry, ageing, the inner worlds of older women, the end-of-life, unseen worlds, and spirit realms, while examining artistic labour and what gets to be called art. Salty is the 2024 recipient of the Chamberlain Award for social practice artists from the Headlands Centre for the Arts and the 2025 Arts Research Scholar-in-Residence at Nanyang Academy of Fine Art - University of the Arts Singapore.

filmhouse.title: Oldboy - 4K Restoration
filmhouse.description: Long before Parasite and Squid Game hijacked global pop culture, Park Chan-wook’s operatic, Cannes-winning masterpiece completely redefined what a thriller could be. Don't miss out this re-release of the 4k restoration, for a limited time only! Oh Dae-su is abruptly kidnapped off the street and locked in a windowless hotel room for 15 years with no explanation. Just as suddenly, he is released, given a suit, a cell phone, and exactly five days to figure out who ruined his life and why. What follows is a pitch-black, hyper violent journey to the absolute brink of psychological vengeance. In Korean with English subtitles. Rated R21 for Mature Themes. TW: Contains themes of Sexual Violence.

filmhouse.title: Tony
filmhouse.description: Discover how the iconic Anthony Bourdain came to be in Matt Johnson’s scrappy coming-of-age comedy that's equal parts sweet and sour. Long before he became the world’s favorite culinary storyteller, Anthony Bourdain was just a dishwashing kid getting baptized in the grease, sweat, and chaos of a 1970s coastal seafood shack. This electric origin story follows a young Tony (Dominic Sessa) as he gets thrown into the fire of a cutthroat kitchen brigade. Surrounded by foul-mouthed line cooks, late-night vices, and non-stop pressure, a reckless teenager stumbles into the raw grit and rock-and-roll pulse that defined his entire legacy. In English with English subtitles. Rated M18 for Coarse Language and Drug Use. The film contains an utterance of religious profanity that exceeds IMDA guidelines. The line has been muted by the distributor to be kept in line with guidelines.

filmhouse.title: Dear You (Teochew)
filmhouse.description: Teochew grandma Ye Shurou had always lived a peaceful, quiet life, enjoying her twilight years. Burdened by heavy debts, her grandson Xiaowei left for Thailand without telling the family, searching for his rumored billionaire grandfather, Zheng Musheng. However, Xiaowei ultimately returned with a shocking revelation that rocked the entire family: his grandfather had passed away long ago, and the person who had been exchanging romantic letters with Grandma all these years was actually a complete stranger. As Xiaowei dug deeper, a hidden, half-century-old love story suddenly came to light, striking deep into Grandma's heart. In Teochew with English and Chinese subtitles. Corresponding Rated PG13 for Some Coarse Language. This is an edited version of the film, “Dear You”, where the use of strong coarse language in both the dialogue and subtitles has been removed by the distributor. Teochew Cultural Movie Showcase: DEAR YOU

filmhouse.title: Memories of Origin: Hiroshi Sugimoto
filmhouse.description: This documentary follows 200 days in the life of contemporary artist Hiroshi Sugimoto— a leading presence in the world of modern art. He is the winner of many prestigious awards and his photographs are sold for millions of yen at overseas auctions. The film shows the sites of the Architecture series shot in southern France, the huge installation art work at 17th Biennale of Sydney, his new work Mathematics at Provence, his art studio while working on Lightning Fields, and more. It thoroughly pursues the question Sugimoto's works pose - "living in modern times, what are these works trying to tell us?" A thrilling look into the world of Hiroshi Sugimoto. Presenting CINEMATIC VOIDS : a curated film series in collaboration with Singapore Art Museum , accompanying the ongoing exhibition ‘ Hiroshi Sugimoto: Form Is Emptiness’ In Japanese with English subtitles. Rated PG.

filmhouse.title: La La Land (10th Anniversary)
filmhouse.description: Mia, an aspiring actress, serves lattes to movie stars in between auditions and Sebastian, a jazz musician, scrapes by playing cocktail party gigs in dingy bars, but as success mounts they are faced with decisions that begin to fray the fragile fabric of their love affair, and the dreams they worked so hard to maintain in each other threaten to rip them apart. In English with Mandarin Subtitles Rated PG13 for Some Coarse Language

filmhouse.title: Mysterious Skin (4K Restoration)
filmhouse.description: A teenage hustler and a young man obsessed with alien abductions cross paths, together discovering a horrible, liberating truth. Join us on 11 September in the Foyer for a Listening Party! Come by and soak in the lush music of MYSTERIOUS SKIN. We’re featuring the film’s evocative soundtrack, a deep cut collaboration between Robin Guthrie (Cocteau Twins) and Harold Budd, as well as tracks from shoegazers, Slowdive and Sigur Ros. Plus every one who comes receives a free complimentary MYSTERIOUS SKIN OST CD Keychain, which links out via NFC to the music, so you can take it home with you. Free RSVP Here! In English with English subtitles. Rated R21 for Mature Theme. TW: Contains themes of Sexual Violence.

filmhouse.title: Before Sunrise
filmhouse.description: An unexpected meeting on a train leads two travelers to spend an evening wandering through Vienna. As the night unfolds, they share stories and conversations about life and love, exploring new ideas while a quiet intimacy grows between them, knowing it may be their only night together. In English. Rated NC16.

filmhouse.title: Trainspotting (4K Restoration)
filmhouse.description: Danny Boyle's decade-defining adaptation of Irvine Welsh's Trainspotting celebrates its 30th anniversary in 2026, and is heading back to Filmhouse from 21 August in a 4K restoration as part of our Music In Film showcase! Ewan McGregor stars as Mark Renton, the most reflective member of a group that also includes the compulsive womaniser, Sick Boy (Jonny Lee Miller), and the hapless Spud (Ewen Bremner). Renton, Spud and Sick Boy's issues with drugs alternatively irritate and amuse their friend, Begbie (Robert Carlyle), a periodic psychopath whose outbursts of violence are one of the many factors that convince Renton to leave for London in the hope of starting a new life. Renton enjoys some success remoulding himself as an estate agent in the English capital, but it isn't long before his Edinburgh friends catch up with him. Begbie and co. need the money Renton has saved from his job to finance the drug deal that could make them all rich... In English. Rated R21 for Drug Use and Sexual Scenes

filmhouse.title: Amoeba
filmhouse.description: At an authoritarian all-girls school, four misfit teens form a secret gang. Their fumbling rebellion unearths buried desires and the quiet violence of growing up in contemporary Singapore. In English with English and Mandarin dual subtitles. Rated R21 for Mature Content. 6 Wins & 14 Nominations including: Golden Horse Film Festival 2025 FIPRESCI Prize Winner

filmhouse.title: Taste of Cherry
filmhouse.description: A man drives around Tehran searching for someone to bury him after he takes his own life. Along the way, he meets strangers who each try, in their own way, to talk him out of it. Taste of Cherry, Abbas Kiarostami’s most recognised work, won't let you down with the simple yet profound journey it takes you on. Presenting CINEMATIC VOIDS : a curated film series in collaboration with Singapore Art Museum , accompanying the ongoing exhibition ‘ Hiroshi Sugimoto: Form Is Emptiness ’ In Persian with English subtitles Rated PG13 for Some Mature Content.

filmhouse.title: We Are All Strangers
filmhouse.description: A life-altering event forces 21-year-old Junyang and his girlfriend to face reality. At the same time, while Junyang’s father is struggling to hold their modest life together, a woman enters his life and both generations are forced to redefine their family. Cast Q&A, Sun 6 Sep Join us for an in-person Q&A with Cast Members, Andi Lim, Koh Jia Ler and Regene Lim, moderated by Petrina Kow. In Mandarin and English with English and Mandarin subtitles. Rated PG13 for Some Coarse Language and Sexual References. TW: Contains scenes with flashing lights, photosensitive viewers are advised.

Rated PG.

filmhouse.title: The Invite
filmhouse.description: You’re cordially invited to the most chaotic dinner of the year. Fresh from its buzz heavy Sundance debut, Olivia Wilde’s razor sharp relationship comedy hits right where it hurts. Joe (Seth Rogen) and Angela (Wilde) are stuck in a domestic rut, made worse by the aggressively loud, boundary pushing love life of their upstairs neighbors, Hawk (Edward Norton) and Pina (Penélope Cruz). Hoping to smooth things over, Angela invites them down for a casual dinner party. But as the wine flows, polite small talk is instantly traded for a chaotic, hilariously uncomfortable truth game where social etiquette completely crumbles. In English Rated M18 for Mature Content and Coarse Language.

filmhouse.title: Silent Friend
filmhouse.description: On the grounds of a medieval German university town looms an imposing Ginkgo biloba, a tree whose longevity stands in marked contrast to three intimate, human-scaled stories. In 1908, the university’s first female student gains admission into the prestigious botany department, confronting the sexism of both professors and peers. In 1972, amidst counterculture movements, a reserved student finds his attention captured by a fellow housemate and the geranium plant she studies. In 2020, during the COVID-19 pandemic, a neuroscientist from Hong Kong secures the help of a renowned botanist for an experiment on the old ginkgo tree. In German, Cantonese and English with English subitles. Rated M18 for Some Nudity and Drug Use.

As Xiaowei dug deeper, a hidden, half-century-old love story suddenly came to light, striking deep into Grandma's heart. In Teochew with English and Chinese subtitles. Corresponding Rated PG13 for Some Coarse Language. This is an edited version of the film, “Dear You”, where the use of strong coarse language in both the dialogue and subtitles has been removed by the distributor. Teochew Cultural Movie Showcase: DEAR YOU

filmhouse.title: Trainspotting (4K Restoration)
filmhouse.description: Danny Boyle's decade-defining adaptation of Irvine Welsh's Trainspotting celebrates its 30th anniversary in 2026, and is heading back to Filmhouse from 21 August in a 4K restoration as part of our Music In Film showcase! Ewan McGregor stars as Mark Renton, the most reflective member of a group that also includes the compulsive womaniser, Sick Boy (Jonny Lee Miller), and the hapless Spud (Ewen Bremner). Renton, Spud and Sick Boy's issues with drugs alternatively irritate and amuse their friend, Begbie (Robert Carlyle), a periodic psychopath whose outbursts of violence are one of the many factors that convince Renton to leave for London in the hope of starting a new life. Renton enjoys some success remoulding himself as an estate agent in the English capital, but it isn't long before his Edinburgh friends catch up with him. Begbie and co. need the money Renton has saved from his job to finance the drug deal that could make them all rich... In English. Rated R21 for Drug Use and Sexual Scenes

filmhouse.title: Hope
filmhouse.description: In a quiet coastal village near the South Korean border, bumbling police chief Bum-seok (Hwang Jung-min) and his sharp deputy Sung-ae (Hoyeon) are called to investigate a mauled bull on a rural road. What starts as a local mystery quickly spirals into chaos when an unearthly, incredibly destructive threat descends upon the town. Cut off from outside reinforcements by raging wildfires, Bum-seok and a band of trigger-happy local hunters venture into the surrounding mountains to track the beast, only to find themselves hopelessly outmatched in a fight for survival. Selected in Competition at the Cannes Film Festival, Hope marks the longawaited return of director Na Hong-jin (The Wailing, The Chaser) in South Korea’s most ambitious production to date. Combining creature feature survival action, dark satirical humor, and an international ensemble that includes Alicia Vikander, and Michael Fassbender, Na subverts classic blockbuster tropes with visceral set-pieces and Hong Kyung-pyo’s widescreen cinematography. Shot on an enormous scale with relentless pacing, it is a muscular genre spectacle engineered specifically for the big-screen experience. In Korean with English subtitles. Rated NC16 for Coarse Language and Violence.
